title: Sigil and Oath
premise: Lior Marchetti has spent their life charting the Thornfell mountains for smugglers, hiding the sigil-gift that lets them read the land's hidden paths. When the crown's witch-hunters burn a village of gifted folk, Lior flees with a ragged found family: a disgraced knight, a child who dreams true, and a defector hunter. Together they discover the king is bound to an ancient entity wearing his crown, sustained by harvested gift-bearers, and that Lior's own bloodline wrote the original binding. To end it, Lior must unbind the king at the cost of their own gift — and nearly their life — choosing family over power as the realm's magic finally runs free.
about_author: Theo Crane is a former trail guide who turned to fantasy after a decade of mapping forgotten mountain routes across three continents. They write stories about people who find each other in wild places.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Mark
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior charts a smuggler's pass through Thornfell, secretly using their sigil-gift to read the land's living lines. When they ink a map for a client, the sigils glow faintly — witnessed by a stranger in the tavern. The beat is quiet competence shadowed by fear of exposure.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Dusk
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Crown criers announce the Gift Hunt: all bearers must register or die. The stranger from the tavern turns out to be Serah Vane, a royal hunter, but she hesitates before arresting Lior. Emotional beat: the safe world closing in, and an unexpected flicker of mercy.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. News arrives that Hollowmere, a village of registered gift-bearers, has burned. Among the refugees Lior finds Pip, an orphan whose prophetic dreams led hunters straight to her neighbors. Beat: grief hardening into resolve; Lior takes the child in.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain Corvath, once the king's shield-knight, hides in Thornfell after refusing to burn Hollowmere. He intercepts Lior's caravan to warn them of Vane's patrol — then chooses exile over duty. Beat: a man trading honor for conscience, meeting his future family.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The fugitives flee through unmapped caverns only Lior's gift can navigate. Pip dreams of a crown made of teeth. Vane tracks them but loses the trail, unsettled by what she saw in Hollowmere's ashes. Beat: fragile trust forming under pressure.

chapters.title: What Pip Dreamed
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Through the child's eyes: nightmares of the king screaming inside his own body, of a thing feeding beneath the palace. She draws the binding sigil without knowing what it is. Beat: innocence bearing terrible knowledge; Lior recognizes the sigil as their family's work.

chapters.title: The Marchetti Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In a ruined waystation, Lior finds their grandmother's journal: the Marchettis bound the king generations ago to stop a devouring god, and every bearer since has fed it. Beat: inheritance revealed as both burden and crime — Lior's blood built the cage and the leash.

chapters.title: Vane's Doubt
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. Ordered to harvest captured gift-bearers for the crown's 'warding rites,' Vane witnesses the ritual's truth: children drained to sustain the thing in the king. Beat: a loyal soldier's faith cracking; she burns her orders instead of her prisoners.

chapters.title: Sanctum Below
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the journal, the fugitives reach the Underhold, where the original binding was forged. They meet Wren, a half-mad archivist who has kept the true rites alive. Beat: hope with a price — the unbinding requires a Marchetti's willing sacrifice of their gift.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The group argues over the cost. Dain offers himself; the rite refuses him. Lior quietly accepts, hiding it from Pip and Dain. Beat: love expressed through concealment — the first lie within the found family, told out of devotion.

chapters.title: Ambush at Grayford Bridge
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The crown's second hunter, Mallet, corners them at the bridge. Dain holds the span alone; Vane defects mid-battle, cutting down her former partner. Beat: bonds tested in blood — Vane earns her place, Dain is gravely wounded.

chapters.title: Tending Wounds
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. While Dain feverishly heals, Pip keeps watch and dreams the entity's name: Vhalgorren, the Crown-Eater. She tells Lior, who realizes the name matches a sigil in the journal. Beat: tenderness amid dread; the family knitting itself together.

chapters.title: The Capital's Shadow
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane maps the palace's ward-routes from memory while the group debates the impossible approach. Lior discovers a dead road beneath the city — one their gift alone can open. Beat: dread and daring braided together; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Into the Dead Road
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The descent beneath the capital: corridors of fused bone and old magic where Vhalgorren's presence presses on every mind. Pip nearly walks into its pull; Lior anchors her with a hand-drawn sigil. Beat: terror tempered by protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. They surface inside the throne room during a 'warding ceremony.' The king, hollow-eyed, begs Dain silently for death even as Vhalgorren speaks through his mouth. Beat: horror and pity entwined — the enemy wears a suffering man.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mallet, surviving Grayford, captures Pip and offers a trade: Lior's surrender for the child. Lior agrees — and Vane and Dain refuse to let them go alone. Beat: the found family refusing the arithmetic of sacrifice; unity forged in defiance.

chapters.title: Chains of the First Binding
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Brought before the crown, Lior is forced to begin a renewal of the binding — which would consume Pip. Instead, Lior secretly inverts the sigils, turning the ritual toward unbinding. Beat: quiet rebellion; the cartographer redrawing the map from within.

chapters.title: Vhalgorren Unmasked
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The entity sheds the king like a garment, revealing itself: vast, hungry, wearing centuries of stolen gifts. It offers Lior unlimited power in exchange for the binding's renewal. Beat: temptation at full strength — corruption offering itself as salvation.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. With Dain holding the line, Vane breaking the wards, and Pip's dream-sight guiding each stroke, Lior unravels the Marchetti binding, pouring their own gift into the unraveling. Vhalgorren, starved of its anchor, tears free and dissolves. Beat: triumph purchased with everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The king, freed, is a broken old man who abdicates. Lior survives but cannot feel the land's lines anymore — the world has gone mute to them. Beat: hollow victory; grief for the gift that defined them.

chapters.title: A New Map
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Weeks later, the family settles in rebuilt Hollowmere. Pip asks Lior to teach her ordinary mapmaking. Lior discovers faint new lines stirring — not the old gift, something gentler, shared. Beat: healing; inheritance transformed rather than destroyed.

chapters.title: Sigil and Oath
chapters.summary: Full-circle epilogue, Lior's POV. One year on, Lior inks a public atlas of Thornfell's real roads, gifting it freely. The family takes an oath on the first page: no gift shall ever again be owned by a crown. Beat: warm resolution — power tamed by belonging.
